options.text: A physical mark left by your device on the internet
The collection of data and information about you that exists online due to your internet activities
Only the social media accounts you create
A temporary record of your online searches that disappears after a day

correct_answer.text: The collection of data and information about you that exists online due to your internet activities

questions.question_text: What is the difference between an active and a passive digital footprint?

options.text: Active is what you delete online, while passive is what you post
Active is what you choose to share, like posts, while passive is data collected without your direct input, like search history
Active is only on social media, while passive is only on websites
Active is private, while passive is public

correct_answer.text: Active is what you choose to share, like posts, while passive is data collected without your direct input, like search history

questions.question_text: How can your online actions leave a trace in your digital footprint?

options.text: Only through posts you share on social media
Through likes, comments, searches, location data, and tagged content, even if you delete them later
Only if you use public Wi-Fi to access the internet
Only if you give permission for websites to track you

correct_answer.text: Through likes, comments, searches, location data, and tagged content, even if you delete them later

questions.question_text: Why is assessing your current digital footprint important for teens?

options.text: It helps you get more followers on social media
It lets you see what’s online about you and if it matches the personal brand you want to build
It guarantees that nothing bad will ever show up online
It’s only necessary if you’re applying for a job right now

correct_answer.text: It lets you see what’s online about you and if it matches the personal brand you want to build
